
<h1>How To Run Local Tests</h1>

The system can use the Azure emulator Azurite to run tests locally on Linux.
Version 3.6.0 or newer, or the latest code from the "master" branch is 
required.

<h2>1. Install Local Node.js System </h2>

Download a node.js binary package from:
  
  [https://nodejs.org/en/]

e.g.

  [https://nodejs.org/dist/v12.16.1/node-v12.16.1-linux-x64.tar.xz]

Unpack the archive somewhere and add the "bin" sub-directory to the 
users PATH.  e.g.

<pre>
     PATH=~/node-v12.16.1-linux-x64/bin:$PATH 
</pre>

Also set environment variable NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX to a location that will be
used to install Azurite. And add the "bin" sub-directory of it to the users
PATH as well:

<pre>
     export NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX=~/.npm-global
     PATH=$NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX/bin:$PATH
</pre>

<h2>2. Install Azurite </h2>

Obtain sufficiently new code with the following or similar:

<pre>
     git clone https://github.com/Azure/Azurite.git 
</pre>

Then, in the source directory:

<pre>
     npm ci
     npm run build
     npm install -g
</pre>

And to check that it installed:

<pre>
     azurite version
</pre>

<h2>3. Run The Azurite Tests </h2>

Build the blockcachevfsd binaries with:

<pre>
     ../blockcachevfs/configure && make all
</pre>

Start the azurite emulator in an empty directory:

<pre>
     azurite
</pre>

Run the test/runtests.tcl script from the blockcachevfs build directory using 'bcvtclsqlite". e.g.

<pre>
     ./bcvtclsqlite ../blockcachevfs/test/runtests.tcl
</pre>
